record.original_question: Given a group Gamma, for which integers k >= 1 and n >= 3 is Gamma the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope or maniplex of rank n?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Given a group Γ, what are the numbers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3 such that Γ is the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope or maniplex of rank n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) are graded by ranks in {-1, 0, ..., n}, satisfying the standard axioms: it has a unique minimum face and unique maximum face, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 faces, it is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any face F of rank i-1 and any face H of rank i+1 with F<H, there are exactly two faces G of rank i with F<G<H). More generally, a maniplex of rank n is a connected, n-edge-colored, n-regular graph in which, for any two distinct colors i and j with |i-j|>1, every connected component of the subgraph induced by edges of colors i and j is a 4-cycle; the vertices play the role of flags. The automorphism group Γ(M) of a polytope or maniplex M consists of the color- and incidence-preserving bijections (equivalently, automorphisms of its flag graph), and it acts freely on flags. The number of orbits of Γ(M) on flags is called the number of flag orbits; M is called a k-orbit polytope (resp. maniplex) of rank n if it has rank n and exactly k flag orbits.

Problem. Given an abstract group Γ, determine the set of pairs (k, n) with k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3 such that there exists a k-orbit abstract polytope (respectively, k-orbit maniplex) of rank n whose automorphism group is isomorphic to Γ.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem appears open. Partial progress exists: characterizations of automorphism groups are known mainly for small k (regular k=1 and chiral k=2), with recent work extending tools for k=3 (e.g., 3-orbit polyhedra) and a general coset-geometry characterization of automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes. Targeted constructions prescribing automorphism groups for polytopes have been given, but a complete answer for arbitrary Γ, all k≥1 and all n≥3 has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizations of automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes were known only for k<3; this paper extends to k=3.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial characterizations exist; recent work tackles k=3.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes via coset geometries.
status_evidence.claim: General structural characterization exists, but the prescribed-group realization question for all (k,n) is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Prescribing Symmetries and Automorphisms for Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs polytopes with prescribed automorphism groups in specific settings.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on prescribing automorphism groups for polytopes.
